transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because I keep making these really dumb mistakes at work, mostly on my sales reports. I supervise a sales team, and I'll do things like copy the wrong numbers right off our team dashboard, or I'll just completely miss a line in a procedure I was supposed to check. The frustrating part is it happens even when I thought I just went over everything carefully. It's just becoming a real issue for me.
Do you find that you have these same kinds of difficulties staying focused or making careless mistakes when you are at home or during your personal time?

I'm honestly not sure if it happens at home as much. I mean, I guess I haven't really noticed making those kinds of mistakes in my personal time, but then again, I don't really have to do reports or anything like that outside of work. So, I don't know if I'm just not seeing it or if it's really just a work thing.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, do you remember having similar struggles with staying focused or being prone to careless mistakes?

Yeah, I was definitely like this as a kid, too. Honestly, my mom still talks about the notes my teachers used to send home back in elementary school. They were always saying that I rushed through my work or lost my homework. And... well, they also said I talked out of turn a lot, and that I couldn't just stay in my seat without being reminded. So, yeah, it definitely goes back a long way.
